title: Major David Hockney print exhibition opens at National Gallery of Australia
summary: The National Gallery of Australia presents a rare opportunity to experience over 50 prints by one of the most celebrated artists of the 20th and 21st centuries, David Hockney. David Hockney: Portraits in Print will be on display in Kamberri/Canberra from 5 September 2026 – 14 February 2027, offering an intimate view of renowned artist David Hockney’s (1937–2026) personal life, creative practice, and deep engagement with portraiture and printmaking. Portraiture was an ongoing and compelling part of Hockney’s extraordinary creative practice. Through more than 50 works drawn from the national collection that span nearly 30 years, David Hockney: Portraits in Print traces how the artist documented his own life and closest relationships. From small prints to larger scale works, the portraits capture the people and cultural environments Hockney discovered in Los Angeles, Paris and London, cities he lived in during the 1970s and 1980s. title: Portland Art Museum opens major Australian Indigenous art exhibition
summary: The Portland Art Museum is presenting the only West Coast presentation of The Stars We Do Not See: Australian Indigenous Art, the largest exhibition of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander art ever presented in North America. Organized by the National Gallery of Victoria (NGV) in Melbourne and the National Gallery of Art in Washington, D.C., the landmark exhibition will be on view at PAM from September 5, 2026, through January 3, 2027. The exhibition is the outcome of a unique cultural partnership between the National Gallery of Art and the NGV, which will facilitate the global exchange of artworks from the NGV’s permanent collection. title: Fotomuseum Den Haag presents major Eva Besnyö retrospective
summary: Photographer Eva Besnyö (1910 – 2003) not only bore witness to but served as a driving force behind the emancipation of photography. Together with her contemporaries, she experimented freely with a new visual language, one that moved away from painting and towards reality, with a real sense of dynamism and immediacy. This autumn, Fotomuseum Den Haag presents one of the largest-ever retrospectives of Eva Besnyö’s work. It has been assembled from photographs found in the museum’s own collection, the largest group of her works in the world. Set against the backdrop of a radically-changing Europe, the exhibition follows the course of Besnyö’s life: from her first experiences with the camera in Budapest and her formative years in the gritty Berlin of the 1930s, to her life and career in Bergen and later Amsterdam, where she was part of a progressive creative circle. title: Jeffrey Deitch & Pace Gallery will present Kiki Smith solo exhibition in LA this October
summary: Jeffrey Deitch and Pace Gallery will present Untethered Journey, an exhibition of historical and recent works by Kiki Smith, at Deitch’s gallery at 925 N Orange Drive in Los Angeles from October 30, 2026, through January 23, 2027. Marking Smith’s first solo show in the city in thirty years, the exhibition will provide an overview of her rigorous, provocative, and poetic practice. Smith, who began her career in the 1980s, is celebrated for her materially wide-ranging practice exploring the interconnection of the human body and the natural world. Throughout sculpture, drawing, glasswork, printmaking, and textile, among other forms, Smith’s work takes both a spiritual and psychologically charged approach to ideas of mortality, regeneration, and gender politics. title: Michael Brown solo retrospective Keep On Truckin' opens at Marc Straus
summary: The gallery will present Keep On Truckin', a solo retrospective of works by American artist Michael Brown. Spanning nearly two decades of artistic effort, the exhibition places early sculptural works from the mid-2000s in direct conversation with a new body of paintings created for this exhibition. The exhibition takes its title from the phrase popularized by cartoonist R. Crumb, whose 1968 one-page comic “Keep On Truckin’,” first published in Zap Comix, became an emblem of American counterculture. Crumb’s cartoon is a visual riff on the lyrics of Blind Boy Fuller’s song “Truckin’ My Blues Away,” depicting a procession of men striding across shifting landscapes, an image so widely reproduced and reimagined that it outgrew the page and became folklore in its own right. title: Rebecca Ward explores light, structure, and material in fifth solo show at Ronchini
summary: Ronchini is presenting lighter later, an exhibition of all-new works by Brooklyn-based artist Rebecca Ward, marking the artist’s fifth solo show with the gallery. Ward’s practice operates at the intersection of painting, sculpture and craft, uprooting conventional distinctions between medium, surface and structure. Over the past decade, Ward has garnered critical acclaim for her sewn and deconstructed canvases. She produces geometrically grounded compositions distinguished by a visual language that foregrounds process, materiality and spatial harmony. Emerging through a sustained dialogue between the digital and handmade, Ward’s works are realised through a meticulous and labour intensive process. Compositions are first developed digitally before being re-articulated in pastel on graph paper. title: Thaddaeus Ropac Paris Marais presents Talisman exhibition by Ali Banisadr
summary: Thaddaeus Ropac Paris Marais presents Talisman, an exhibition of new works by Tehran-born, New York-based artist Ali Banisadr. Spanning paintings, sculpture and pastels, the exhibition brings together the central languages of Banisadr’s practice: densely orchestrated pictorial worlds, archetypal figures, symbolic fragments and charged objects that seem to carry memory across time. Running concurrently with Banisadr’s exhibition at the Musée national Gustave Moreau, Paris, opening on 9 September until 7 December 2026, Talisman unfolds in dialogue with the French Symbolist master, whose work has become a key point of reference for this new body of work. Talismans are charged objects: vessels of protection, transformation and transmission. For Banisadr, imagery can operate in the same way. title: Brazilian artists explore transformation at first Brazil Pavilion at Gwangju Biennale
summary: Four artists associated with Rio de Janeiro gallery A Gentil Carioca are participating in the 16th Gwangju Biennale as part of the first Brazilian Pavilion ever presented at the influential South Korean exhibition. Marcela Cantuária, Mariana Rocha, Vinicius Gerheim and Vivian Caccuri are included in “Devorações do Amanhã – Brasil em Rebento” — translated as “Devourings of Tomorrow – Brazil Sprouting” — a group exhibition that looks at contemporary Brazil not as something fixed, but as a place continually being formed, challenged and reinvented. Curated by Aldones Nino and Bruna Levi, the project brings together artists from different generations and takes the ideas of “devouring” and “sprouting” as starting points for thinking about transformation, continuity and creation. title: Exhibition features the incredible true story of World War II's combat con artists
summary: The New York State Museum today announced Ghost Army: The Combat Con Artists of World War II, a new temporary exhibition revealing the extraordinary story of a top-secret U.S. Army unit that turned art, engineering, sound, and showmanship into weapons of war. On view September 5 through December 27, the traveling exhibition brings visitors inside the world of the 23rd Headquarters Special Troops, an elite tactical deception unit activated by the U.S. Army on January 20, 1944. During the final year of World War II, more than 1,000 soldiers, including artists, engineers, radio operators, and sound technicians, used inflatable rubber tanks, fabricated radio transmissions, recorded sound effects, and carefully staged visual illusions to convince enemy forces that large American combat units were stationed where they were not. title: Documentary The Art of Adventure sets US theatrical release dates
summary: From Alison Reid, the director of the critically acclaimed documentary about the late and beloved zoologist Anne Innis Dagg, The Woman Who Loves Giraffes, comes her latest feature documentary, THE ART OF ADVENTURE. An exhilarating road-trip film and a heartfelt love letter to the natural world, The Art of Adventure is an inspiring and deeply human documentary about the extraordinary lifelong friendship between world renowned wildlife artist Robert Bateman and fearless biologist Bristol Foster. Following festival acclaim and a Canadian release, The Art of Adventure roves its way into the United States with engagements in Washington, DC at The Avalon on Oct. 7; in New York City at New Plaza Cinema on Oct. 11; in Chatham, NY at FilmColumbia Film Festival at Crandell Theatre on Oct. 17; in Newport, RI at

title: Taiwan Pavilion opens at 16th Gwangju Biennale with focus on geopolitics and technology
summary: The Taiwan Pavilion of the 16th Gwangju Biennale, Instance Dungeons: Gray Zone, opened on September 5, 2026 at the National Asian Culture Center (ACC) in Gwangju, South Korea, and will run through November 15. The opening drew a large crowd of directors, curators, artists, and members of the press from arts institutions around the world, all bearing witness to the Taiwan Pavilion’s latest presentation on the international biennial stage. Director of the National Taiwan Museum of Fine Arts (NTMoFA), CHEN Kuang-Yi, remarked that it was a pleasure to join the opening of the Taiwan Pavilion's Instance Dungeons: Gray Zone here in Gwangju. “The ‘gray zone’ is not a place where answers are unclear—on the contrary, it is precisely where we must remain sensitive, reflective, and discerning. title: Houston Center for Contemporary Craft marks 25th anniversary with silver exhibition
summary: In celebration of its 25th "silver" anniversary, Houston Center for Contemporary Craft (HCCC) presents A Material Inheritance, a group exhibition that examines silver as material and metaphor. The most reflective element on Earth, silver has transformed the ways in which humans perceive, record, and understand the world. It is the material through which cultures have learned to see and remember themselves. Its exceptional optical and metallurgical properties made possible advances in mirror-making, photography, and scientific instrumentation, while its weight, density, and malleability established it as a prime medium for currency, ceremonial objects, jewelry, and treasured heirlooms. Looking beyond the material’s status as a precious metal, the exhibition considers how silver has shaped systems of knowledge, value, and cultural exchange across centuries and continents. title: David Nolan Gallery presents Valerio Adami's first New York exhibition in nearly 25 years
summary: David Nolan Gallery will present Alice in the Land of Violence, an exhibition of drawings and paintings by Valerio Adami from the 1960s, a period of great international success for the artist, whose work was highlighted at the Venice Biennale, and at Documenta III. Adami returns to New York City after nearly twenty-five years, and we are honored to present his work. The exhibition brings together a body of work created between 1962-1967, before Adami arrived at his signature graphic, hard-edged style. Raw and exuberant, these works move between fantasy and reality, embracing the postwar era’s high fashion, automobiles, and commercial culture. The exhibition takes its title from one of the works on view. title: Messums West presents FLOOD group exhibition curated by OHSH Projects
summary: Messums West presents FLOOD, a major group exhibition curated by OHSH Projects, bringing together painting, sculpture and installation to explore one of humanity’s oldest and most enduring stories. It endeavours to represent and help us to consider what survives when the world we know has been swept away. It is the understanding of the importance of recreation and survival. This exhibition approaches the FLOOD not as a singular event, but as an archetype. Across sculpture, painting and installation, the artists presented here draw on mythic forms, instinctive mark-making and material transformation to explore how images of upheaval persist beyond lived experience. Figures emerge and dissolve, surfaces fracture, and gestures repeat, suggesting a visual language shaped as much by inheritance as by observation. Sophia Olver

title: Images Vevey opens 10th edition exploring theme of family
summary: Ten editions and eighteen years on, Switzerland's visual arts biennial Images Vevey places its anniversary under the sign of family, borrowing its title from the Sister Sledge hit. From 5 to 27 September, some fifty tailor-made photographic installations — all free of charge — turn Vevey into a city of images. Highlights include a monumental 1000 m² portrait of Grace Jones by Anoush Abrar, JR's photo booth truck during the opening weekend, the first-ever public opening of the Château de l'Aile gardens, and Richard Billingham's Ray's a Laugh thirty years on, marking the bicentenary of photography. For its 10th edition, the Biennale Images Vevey explores the notion of family in a broad, living, contemporary and at times deliberately unexpected sense. title: Curtiss Jacobs Gallery presents Ransome solo exhibition A Little Sugar in My Bowl
summary: Curtiss Jacobs Gallery will present A Little Sugar in My Bowl, a new exhibition of works by Ransome, opening Sunday, September 13. Rooted in his own African American family history, Ransome has developed a deeply personal visual language through which the stories of one family become part of a much larger story of Black America. His lineage reaches back to Southern sharecroppers and forward through the Great Migration, but these paintings refuse to allow struggle to become the entirety of that history. Instead, Ransome asks us to look at what Black families created, protected and carried with them: love, beauty, dignity, style, humor, aspiration, intimacy, memory and joy. title: Trisha Brown's gravity-defying dance returns to Berlin for Neue Nationalgalerie's PERFORM! festival
summary: The Neue Nationalgalerie will once again turn its celebrated Mies van der Rohe building into a stage this September, bringing dance, performance and architecture together for the fifth edition of PERFORM!, its annual performance art festival held during Berlin Art Week. Running from September 9 through 13, the 2026 programme is anchored by a landmark of postmodern dance: Trisha Brown's Walking on the Wall, first performed at New York's Whitney Museum of American Art in 1971. More than half a century later, the work will be restaged against one of modern architecture's most recognizable settings—the glass façade of the Neue Nationalgalerie. title: Kin Museum of Contemporary Art presents first Johan Turi exhibition in a century
summary: With his pencils and colors and his keen powers of observation, the legendary Sámi artist, writer, and philosopher Johan Turi (1854–1936) left future generations a unique visual record of work, love, and life in Sápmi. This remarkable historical legacy is receiving renewed attention as the Truth Commission for the Sámi People in Sweden submits its final report to the Swedish Ministry of Culture on September 30, 2026. Kin Museum of Contemporary Art’s major fall exhibition marks the first presentation of Turi’s artistic work in almost a century. Best known as the first Sámi author through his groundbreaking book Muitalus sámiid birra (An Account of the Sámi, 1910), Turi also created a fascinating and richly detailed visual world depicting everyday life in northern Sápmi. title: Museum of Craft and Design presents landmark OBJECTS: USA exhibition
summary: The Museum of Craft and Design is presenting OBJECTS: USA, on view September 5, 2026 through January 17, 2027. Organized in partnership with R & Company, a leading New York design gallery, the exhibition revisits one of the most influential craft exhibitions ever staged and examines its enduring impact on American craft, material culture, and contemporary design around the world. In 1969, the Smithsonian debuted OBJECTS: USA, a landmark exhibition that brought unprecedented attention to American studio craft. Featuring artists working across clay, fiber, glass, metal, wood, enamel, and mosaic, the exhibition traveled widely and helped establish the studio craft movement as a vital force within American culture. title: Hayward Gallery hosts Musquiqui Chihying exhibition on AI and digital technology
summary: The Hayward Gallery presents Musquiqui Chihying: A Life of Navigation. This marks the artist’s first solo exhibition in a public institution in the UK and the seventh exhibition in the RC Foundation Project Space Exhibition Series, which showcases the next generation of emerging international artists. As part of the Southbank Centre’s 75th anniversary programme, Musquiqui Chihying: A Life of Navigation takes place in the HENI Project Space in the Southbank Centre’s Hayward Gallery – a space that offers the opportunity for audiences to discover exhibitions from new artistic voices for free. Musquiqui Chihying is a Taiwanese artist whose work explores our ambiguous relationship with both analogue and digital technologies through installation, video, photography, and sculpture. title: Brazilian museum presents major survey of Antiguan artist Frank Walter
summary: Frank Walter: The Philosophy of Color is the first museum exhibition of Frank Walter’s work (1926–2009) in Brazil. On view now at MAC_BAHIA – Museu de Arte Contemporânea da Bahia, in Salvador, the exhibition is curated by Daniel Rangel and Barbara Paca. The choice of Salvador to host the show relates to the prominent role of African culture and the African diaspora in the formation of Bahia’s capital, as well as to its landscape, which resonates with the spaces observed and imagined throughout the artist’s work. The exhibition brings together a broad selection of works, encompassing different paths developed by Walter throughout his practice: landscapes, which reveal his close attention to the natural world; figurative works featuring fantastic beings, self-portraits, scenes of Caribbean social life, representations of different indigenous peoples

title: New York Historical exhibition explores 1970s origins of punk, disco, and hip hop
summary: Taking visitors back to a decade when the new music genres of punk, disco, and hip hop sprang up in New York City and then exploded across the world, The New York Historical presents its new exhibition, You Should Be Dancing: New York, 1976 and Beyond. On view October 2, 2026 – April 4, 2027, the exhibition explores how, in a time of financial crisis, New York City cultivated a new generation of creativity and celebration. Featuring musical instruments, performance gear, fashion items, period photographs, albums, flyers, and posters presented within spaces reminiscent of the clubs, bars, and gathering places of the time, You Should Be Dancing illustrates the lasting impact this era has had on American culture at large. “New York City in the 1970s was an era of contradictions as economic conditions worsened while creativity soared

title: New Sydney exhibition honours Albert Namatjira and his artistic legacy
summary: Sullivan+Strumpf will present By The Grace of God, a powerful First Nations exhibition honouring Albert Namatjira and his enduring legacy, opening at their Gadigal/ Sydney gallery Thursday 17 September 2026. Named for the biblical quote, once used to frame Namatjira’s identity within a colonial religious narrative, By the Grace of God brings together new works by acclaimed First Nations artist, curator and cultural ambassador, Tony Albert, renowned artists from the Iltja Ntjarra (Many Hands) Art Centre and the Hermannsburg Potters, in a multi-faceted exploration of the layered intersections of faith, cultural identity, history and artistic practice that Namatjira so powerfully embodied. title: Ehrlich Steinberg presents a solo exhibition by Jeffrey Stuker
summary: Ehrlich Steinberg will present L-għajn, a solo exhibition by Los Angeles–based artist Jeffrey Stuker, comprising a new moving image work, two works on paper, and a limited edition publication. The exhibition centers on Stuker’s new film, L-għajn, his most ambitious and expansive work to date. Developed over an extended period living and working in Malta, the film brings together strands of historical, scientific, technological, and autobiographical research that have occupied the artist’s practice for more than a decade. L-għajn extends Stuker’s research into the history of the simulated image—its earliest hardware, the development of the algorithms that made it possible, and its anticipation in mytho-religious practices predating technological modernity.
